# `max-properties-decreased`

maxProperties decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `max-properties-decreased` (both directions), `max-properties-decreased-in-request`, `max-properties-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`maxProperties` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: objects with more properties are now rejected. In responses: clients receive objects with fewer properties, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`max-properties-decreased`](../../test/cases/max-properties-decreased/): maxProperties lowered on a request object.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-       maxProperties: 10
+       maxProperties: 5
```

Findings:

- `max-properties-decreased-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  max-properties-decreased: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the old maximum in requests.
